clue.text: Our lord set the fashion and commanded all

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A nobleman launched a new trend and was in charge of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set the fashion' reads as one phrase, but 'set the' is part of the fodder and 'fashion' alone is the anagram signal, rearranging OURLORDSETTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule the roost is an idiom for being the boss, so it means having command over everyone.

clue.text: Prepared military budget?

explanation.walkthrough: READY is slang for cash, so 'ready for action' is playfully a fund for the forces; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set for action means prepared; read whimsically, ready (cash) for action is money set aside for fighting.

clue.text: Drew left university looking embarrassed

parts.note: red-faced, so red describes someone embarrassed

explanation.surface: A student named Drew left college blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' looks like a person's name but is the past tense of draw, meaning attracted or enticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to tempt or entice them, the same as luring.

clue.text: Break up old wreck and bring car alongside

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it apart, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone smashes up an old vehicle and then parks next to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' looks like the instruction, but it is fodder with 'old'; 'wreck' rearranges BREAKUPOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To park beside a car already at the kerb is to leave your vehicle double parked, an illegal stop.

clue.text: Opening effort lacks heart and gets the axe

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a deck or wall

indicators.note: the word effort loses its middle letters, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A half-hearted attempt to start something gets cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the axe' sounds like being sacked; here the axe is the definition, a small chopping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small, short-handled kind of chopping tool.

clue.text: Welsh dish that's underdone, somewhat

parts.note: meat cooked rare is underdone
a bit means somewhat, as in a bit tired

explanation.surface: A diner complains a Welsh meal is slightly undercooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is cheese melted on toast, a traditional dish from Wales.

clue.text: Eject leader from mediaeval tournament

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away from the tournament word

parts.note: a joust was a contest between mounted knights in the Middle Ages

explanation.surface: Throw the champion out of a knightly contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a person in the contest, but it means the first letter, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or force out, the same as to eject.

clue.text: A natural design for a web crawler?

indicators.note: to design is to arrange, so the letters of the opening words are laid out afresh

parts.note: the opening words spelt out, plus the second T the setter needed, are the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Nature has produced the perfect thing to creep across a web.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'A natural' signalled by 'design' is one T short: the setter's slip. 'web crawler' suggests internet software but is a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, a creature that crawls, playfully linked with webs.

clue.text: Rumour of obscure recreational area to turn into London landmark

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard, so the next word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to obscure something is to hide it
a park is a public area for recreation
to corner is to turn at a bend

explanation.surface: Gossip about a hidden leisure spot that becomes famous in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumour of' signals a sound-alike: HIDE (obscure) is spoken like HYDE. Hyde Park Corner is a busy junction by Hyde Park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a famous junction and arch site in the British capital, a well-known feature of the city.

clue.text: Miming music to "the sound of silence"?

definitions.text: Miming music to "the sound of silence"?

parts.words: Miming music to "the sound of silence"?
parts.note: pretending to strum an imaginary instrument makes no sound, so the song title is a joke about silent playing

explanation.surface: Someone performs a mime along to a famous Simon and Garfunkel song.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title points to the song, but the joke is that the miming itself produces only silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumming an imaginary instrument while miming to a track is a familiar party antic.

clue.text: Certainly dropping English can appear ill-tempered

indicators.note: letting the English letter fall out of the word for certainly

parts.note: surely means certainly

explanation.surface: Losing the English language can surely make a person grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A surly person is bad-tempered and rude, so the word is a synonym.

clue.text: Say why poetry student might sing high

indicators.note: to say a word is to speak it, so the next word gives the letter it sounds like

parts.note: the word why, spoken
an ode is a lyrical poem
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Asking why a literature student would burst into a high-pitched song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say why' gives the letter Y, which sounds like 'why'. A learner driver in Britain shows an L-plate, so L stands for student.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is singing that flips rapidly into a high falsetto, as in Alpine song.

clue.text: Tolkien's creatures took bit off hot plates

indicators.note: something taken away, with the next words, means a removal
with took, the small piece is removed from the creatures' name

parts.note: hobbits are the small folk in Tolkien's stories
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fantasy creatures nibbled food from something hot on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took bit off' reads as eating, but tells you to take BIT out of HOBBITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobs are the heated rings on top of a cooker, the cooking plates.

clue.text: Joint king even dropped the regulars

indicators.note: every second letter of the two words is dropped at regular intervals, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: A monarch's joint, and his even temper, have been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'king even' remove the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters, leaving the first, third, fifth and seventh.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge where thigh and shin meet, a leg joint.

clue.text: Improve one's speech after cooked meal

indicators.note: the speaking part comes after the reworked meal
cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word meal is cooked into a new letter order
one is I, the Roman numeral
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Someone gives a speech after dinner to make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges MEAL into AMEL; 'after' places the speech part behind it. 'one's' gives just I: the possessive adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make better or improve a situation.

clue.text: Zero capacity unit positioned to rear of head

parts.note: O looks like zero
cc means cubic centimetres, used for engine capacity
I is one, a single unit
put means placed or positioned

explanation.surface: A vehicle part with no capacity is placed at the back of the bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the anatomical name for the back part of the skull.

clue.text: Ignore the girls with weapons

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
lasses is a word for girls, especially in the north of England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Snub the young women carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlasses are short curved swords, once favoured by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Mature display over apple core found in fish dish

indicators.note: the letters are put on show in a new arrangement
the core of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A ripe show of produce over an apple core turns up in a seafood dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges MATURE plus P, the middle letter of 'apple'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is Japanese battered and deep-fried food, often seafood such as prawns or fish.

clue.text: Exhausted after a tango, got dressed

indicators.note: the word for exhausted follows the first two letters

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tired means exhausted

explanation.surface: Worn out after dancing a tango, someone puts their clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attired is to be clothed, a formal word for dressed.

clue.text: Assert that real changes will come after the last month

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the month

parts.note: December, Dec, is the last month of the year

indicators.note: changes means the letters of real are altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone claims real changes will come at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges REAL into LARE, and 'will come after' places it behind the abbreviated month, read as December.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to state or announce firmly, so it means assert.

clue.text: Fish shortage following cut back

indicators.note: the shortage word follows the turned word
back means the word for cut is read the other way

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A fishery has a shortage after quotas were cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOP into POL. 'shortage' looks like the definition beside 'Fish', but Fish alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollack is a food fish related to the cod.

clue.text: Rule making lions accept two points

indicators.note: the lions' group takes in the points, so they go inside

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions
E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A king of beasts ruling by having the pride agree to two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two points' are compass points, here E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to be in charge of a meeting, to rule over it.

clue.text: Schoolmate made the side

indicators.note: to school is to train or shape, so the letters of mate are reshaped

explanation.surface: A school friend was picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schoolmate' looks like one word, but 'School' is the anagram signal and 'mate' the fodder; 'made the' links to 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, as in picking sides.

clue.text: Expert catching new disease

indicators.note: the expert word catches the letter inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist picks up a new illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' suggests infection, but means one piece goes inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition with spots, loosely called a disease.

clue.text: Get the better of united in nil-nil encounter

indicators.note: the united abbreviation goes inside the two noughts

parts.note: a goalless draw is written 0-0, read as two letter Os
Utd is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Beat a United side in a goalless football match.
explanation.walkthrough: UTD is the usual abbreviation for United in British football club names.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Turn skinhead into an idiot

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for idiot

parts.note: a twit is a fool
the head of skin is its first letter, S

explanation.surface: Turn a shaven-headed youth into a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a youth, but means the first letter of 'skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a turn or rotation.

clue.text: German races in rings

indicators.note: the races sit inside the rings

parts.note: O is ring-shaped, so two rings give two Os
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A German competes in races held inside rings.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT, or Tourist Trophy, is a famous motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's first name.

clue.text: Start working with group

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine being on
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Begin work alongside a team.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant.

clue.text: A race to embrace single male with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the nation word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
I is one, a single

explanation.surface: A people welcome a single man with great keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts I and M inside NATION, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness and spirit, a state of eagerness.

clue.text: How might one find London if fired?

definitions.text: How might one find London if fired?

parts.words: How might one find London if fired?
parts.note: London is nicknamed the Big Smoke, so a finder of the Smoke would be the device that senses a fire

explanation.surface: A puzzle about locating the capital if it were set ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Smoke is an old nickname for London; the device detects the smoke a fire makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A household alarm triggers when it senses fumes from a fire.
